findings.summary: Blog newsletter field and Subscribe button on one row end 2px apart (measured uneven-row, real but tiny). Seen in the two samples that put them side by side; the third stacks the button under the field.

In the blog page close, the email label, field and button sit in a left-aligned block under centered text (one sample stacks the button under the field as well). The reference centers its actions under the statement.
Blog plate captions are weak counts ('3 PARTS', '585 WORDS'); the store's captions ('18 OZ', 'TWILL') say more. Carried over from earlier rounds.

One cart sample stacks items above the checkout form at half width and leaves the right half of the screen empty. The heading is plain and correct, but the layout is looser than the side-by-side samples.
On the dotted bar chart, the value labels sit on top of the ghost dots of the bar in one dashboard sample, so the number touches the dots. The other samples put the value above or below the bar.
A decreasing metric (lead time down) gets a red status dot in one dashboard sample, so a good change reads as bad; the other samples show green.
Holdout landing: the featured-story plate on the customers page repeats the drawing of the first story card below it (measured repeated-drawing, real but small).

notes: Scope: all three samples of blog, commerce, dashboard and settings (the desktop home or main routes, the commerce checkout-error state in all three, settings profile in all three, mobile captures of blog, commerce and the holdouts), the dashboard chart crops and motion frames, and the landing and docs holdouts (home, pricing, customers, signup, changelog desktop; home mobile). I did not open every dark capture or every state capture of every app.

Update goal (iterations.md, rc.5): reached. In all three commerce samples the checkout form keeps its plain '02 / 02 Checkout' heading with mono counter and one-line description, no display statement and no dot field (state-checkout-errors-desktop-light.png, s1, s2 and 081154; mobile checked on s2). The three settings profile screens end on Save/Reset with plain section headings. The rc.4 major is fixed.

Real page closes keep the two-tone close: every blog sample ('Read it first. By email.', 'More to come. Read it first.', 'Get every post. Nothing else.'), the landing holdout on home, pricing and customers ('Your time, back. Try it free.'), all with the mono label above and the dot field behind. The blog and landing closes break only between the two sentences on mobile. This matches the reference's closing statement (p1-desktop-light.png, 'Built for the future. Available today.'). The signup form on the landing holdout correctly gets no statement. The docs holdout has no page close, which is right for its structure.
Regression check against published 1.1.0 and the rc.4 verdict: no blocker or major, nothing worse found. The two-tone close is closer to the reference than the 1.1.0 plain close.

Measured defect, commerce / repeated-drawing (all samples, desktop and mobile): false alarm. Eleven products share eight plate kinds, so a kind repeats only after the eighth, each time with a different caption; no kind sits next to itself.
Measured defect, blog / uneven-row: real, listed as a minor.
Measured defect, docs / clipped-text on the mobile menu-button label (2px): false alarm, the label is not visibly cut in home-mobile-light.png.

Measured defect, landing / clipped-text on hero calendar block times (mobile, 6px): false alarm. The hero stage deliberately crops a wide product screen at 390px, the way the reference crops its product shot; the labels are decoration inside the preview.

Measured defect, landing customers / double-rule (featured plate and its opener line, 0px): false alarm, the plate border meets the opener rule by design and no doubled line shows. repeated-drawing on customers: real for the featured plate and first card (minor above); the eight cards use eight distinct drawings.

Capture artifact, not penalized: the docs sidebar background stops partway down the full-page captures (home and changelog desktop), because the sticky sidebar is laid out at viewport height in the full-page shot.
Known and not re-raised: the blueprints use clean single outlines, not the reference's ribbed tiers. Motion frames (landing bp-dash loop, dashboard chart-in 420ms) run as specified and are subtle.
Scores are descriptive. Verdict basis: no blocker and no major, so the candidate passes.
